searchText: Hello everyone, quick question about the yellow paper, in the *6.2 Execution* (https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf#subsection.6.2) Are the 2 repetitions underlined in blue typos? thanks What do you expect them to be? Why do you think they are typos? I do not understand why the 'to' address for the transaction (T*t*) and the transaction value (T*v*) would be included twice in the tuple Sorry, first glance at tiny subscripts I wasn't seeing that those were the same. I'd open an issue in the yellow paper repository. Looks like a typo. Ok thanks for the confirmation 🙂 Is this the repository I need to open the issue on? https://github.com/ethereum/yellowpaper great thanks issue opened ! it's a bit ridiculous since it's just a typo, but I'm still proud to open my first issue 🥳 Those are not typos: please see the definition of Theta in section 8 "Message Call", Equation (102). Oooh thanks gonna check that right away ! Those 2 are indeed different, not easy to understand that in the equation 63 though thanks for the help <@!583892532644151312> and to bad for my open issue haha Sure. IMHO the Yellow Paper is not optimized for readability unfortunately, but at the moment it's the only formal description of Eth1x. Not too bad. That issue can now serve as documentation for someone who comes along in the future with the same confusion. (if you maybe include the explanation in it when you close the issue) Good idea, I'm editing it right now MEV has been a pretty commonly expressed topic of interest for CDAP applicants. I'm not sure if anyone is planning to try and focus on this, but if you are, I think one thing that may be quite valuable is aggregating all of the proposed solutions that you can find, categorizing and analyzing them, and breaking them down into an easy to consume resource. My guess is that lots of people are going to re-invent the same wheels and potentially waste effort hammering at the same solutions that are either known to be flawed in some way. Hey, has the program officially begun? I honestly think there is a huge scope for information gathering and organization in general. I'm thinking of proposing a "document verkle tries" project. The information about is dispersed over loads of random blogs and hackmds and it's quite hard to find everything. One of the projects I still need to take notes is about this. The same applies for sharding and the separation of shard block proposer and builder which is even being implemented now. Another is data visualization, with the merge we will have a lot of data available to analyze and very little is out there in terms of coherently reporting aggregated data. There are a few projects that would be useful and do not require neither new research nor new implementation since already everything has been done or is on its way, but still would be very useful to document No uniform start date. Everyone may/will move at their own pace and may/will need different amounts of time for each stage. Some have started, some are just getting started, some will start soon
